children: Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR, Financials), a data analytics business that is building itself more and more on enterprise AI, is already worth over $415 billion. That could be just the start, says Daniel Ives.

The former Wedbush analyst has once again stated his belief that Palantir might one day achieve a $1 trillion market capitalization. So that would mean a roughly another 141% growth from where the company is today, assuming its share count remains fairly flat.
That sounds ambitious. It's a possibility that the figures Palantir posted recently clarify, Ives said.
Revenue in the second quarter surged 93 percent to $1.94 billion from a year ago. U.S. commercial sales surged 149% to $764 million, as more companies used Palantir's AI software.
Management now forecasts revenue to be around $8.15 billion in 2026, or nearly 82% increase at the middle. But there's a snag.
Investors are already paying a premium for that growth. Palantir trades at more than 70 times trailing revenue, leaving little opportunity for the corporation to disappoint.
UBS boosted its price estimate to $250 from $220 after engaging with customers and management.

Now Palantir has to do something much harder than demonstrating demand for AI is real. It has to keep expanding fast enough to justify what investors are presently paying for it and eventually make Ives' much higher valuation call seem possible.

title: Palantir's $1 trillion valuation case is back in focus
